title: Advances in Light Injection and Related Techniques for SEM and STEM
content: Electron microscopy has grown ever more advanced as scientists have found creative ways to expand the range of input stimuli and output signals used to study materials under the electron beam. One important way to do this is through the controlled introduction of light into the microscope. Light can be used to heat the sample, provoke phase transitions, induce electronic transitions, and to probe vibrational and plasmonic modes. In most cases, a tightly focused laser spot is preferred to ensure sufficient interaction with the sample and as large a light-induced gradient in properties as possible within the field of view of the electron beam. For example, a tighter laser spot enables a larger thermal gradient in the sample while keeping the overall sample temperature lower. It will also induce stronger, more localized plasmonic or electronic excitations in metals and semiconductors, accessing new length scales and thereby gaining new insights into their physics. However, achieving a tightly focused spot is technically challenging due to the small space between the sample holder's surface and the pole piece of the microscope, often less than 2.5 mm, and the inability to monitor the effect of light injection in traditional ways. This work presents the recent advances and applications developed at Attolight related to focused laser light injection in electron microscopes.
